tasks.description: Note where testers stop or become confused across profile, following, feed and rating/review flows. Prioritise repeated friction over isolated preferences.

tasks.content: Fix blockers found by current testers
tasks.description: Fix regressions and high-impact friction only. Keep scope tight so the first founding-listener wave is not delayed by optional polish.

tasks.content: Track first-session friction for new listeners
tasks.description: Pay attention to onboarding, understanding of Ripple’s purpose, profile setup, following and the first useful feed interaction.
Focus on issues affecting repeat use, community clarity, profile/feed usefulness or trust. Avoid expanding scope into unrelated feature work.
Look for improvement in understanding, return behaviour and use of profiles/feed/follows/ratings. Use the comparison to guide the next product decision.

tasks.content: Maintain a light Ripple content rhythm
tasks.description: Use screenshots, screen recordings, mockups and short explanations of what is changing and why. One strong post in an active week is enough; a second is optional when there is genuinely something worth sharing.

tasks.content: Give the waitlist one or two light nudges per week maximum
tasks.description: Use a Ripple post/story or a personal reshare. If interest is weak, improve the message rather than increasing posting frequency.

tasks.content: Capture useful questions from founder events
tasks.description: After each event, note repeated questions, objections, useful contacts and anything that changes how Ripple should be explained. The goal right now is learning and network-building, not closing funding.
